tagline: Argentina's second city pairs a UNESCO Jesuit quarter and colonial centre with the country's best empanadas and a student-fuelled nightlife in the Sierras' foothills.
overview: Founded in 1573, Córdoba is one of South America's oldest colonial cities and home to the continent's fourth-oldest university. The Jesuit Block and estancias around the city are a UNESCO World Heritage Site, marking where the order ran its schools and ranches.

The centre still wears its history: the cathedral on Plaza San Martín, the Jesuit college next door, and cobbled blocks that fill with students from the university. At night the city turns on — Córdoba is famous for its bars, clubs and cuarteto, the frenetic local dance music born here.

The Sierras de Córdoba begin at the city's edge. Weekend escapes reach the German-style village of Villa General Belgrano — home of Argentina's Oktoberfest — the mountain resorts of the Punilla valley, and lake beaches an hour away.

funFacts.title: ARGENTINA'S OLDEST UNIVERSITY
funFacts.text: The National University of Córdoba was founded by Jesuits in 1613.

funFacts.title: A UNESCO JESUIT TOWN
funFacts.text: The Jesuit Block and six rural estancias form a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

funFacts.title: CUARTETO COUNTRY
funFacts.text: Córdoba invented cuarteto, the piano-and-brass dance music every Argentine wedding plays.

funFacts.title: EMPANADA CAPITAL
funFacts.text: Cordobesa empanadas — baked with beef, potato and egg — are widely rated Argentina's best.

funFacts.title: OKTOBERFEST IN THE ANDES
funFacts.text: Villa General Belgrano, a German-settled village nearby, hosts a famous October beer festival.

funFacts.title: A CITY OF STUDENTS
funFacts.text: One in ten residents is a university student — the city runs on bars and cafés.

funFacts.title: THE RINGING TOWER
funFacts.text: The cathedral's towers blend Indigenous, Baroque and neoclassical styles over 200 years of building.

funFacts.title: A RESISTANCE CITY
funFacts.text: The Cordobazo of 1969, a worker-student uprising, became a landmark in Argentine history.

funFacts.title: CHE GUEVARA'S BOYHOOD
funFacts.text: Che spent his teenage years in nearby Alta Gracia — his house is a museum.

funFacts.title: MOUNTAIN ESCAPES
funFacts.text: Sierra resorts like Carlos Paz are 40 minutes away — the city's escape valve.
